title: Updating to tree-sitter 0.25.0
description:
0.25.0 is a larger release for tree-sitter. As of June 6 2025, they are still rolling out the release across the languages, so instead I opted to update us to 0.24.7 (the last one before 0.25.0) and next time around we can catch up once they update all other language bindings and work out any kinks. Here are some things to be aware of:

https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/releases/tag/v0.25.0
 
- The ABI updated to 15, but the min supported ABI is still 13. This means we won't have to force {treesitter.r} to be updated too, which is good, but we should be aware of what the new ABI unlocks
- "the language name, version, supertype info, and reserved words are added to the parsers"
    - We knew this was coming when I added the `name` argument, so we can try and start to phase it out. Start with removing it entirely from the tree-sitter-r side and then warn, error, etc from our side https://github.com/DavisVaughan/r-tree-sitter/blob/f6755fa410b9391aeb1a812c3495972ca47c4ac3/R/standalone-language.R#L62-L69
    - Figure out if we want to expose anything else
    - Think about what happens if we get an ABI 13 grammar and try to access this info?
- New `ts_node_child_with_descendant`


Other:

- Might be worth introducing a testing only package with a test language to test the bindings (rather than relying on tree-sitter-r, which may break our tests, causing a headache when doing cran releases)

title: Possible bug with node pointers?
description:
Hi Davis, thanks so much for your help thus far! I've encountered an issue which you can hopefully reproduce via simple demo repo at https://github.com/mpadge/r-tree-sitter-test. The README there has all info. As a local reprex here, based on a random CRAN tarball:

``` r
path <- test::dl_tarball ("odbc_1.5.0.tar.gz")

bodies <- test::get_captures (path)
#> Error: Input must point to a valid tree sitter type.
library (test)
bodies <- test::get_captures (path)
#> Error: Input must point to a valid tree sitter type.
```

But then everything works if the full namespace of that package is loaded:
``` r
pkg_path <- "/<local>/<path>/<to>/r-tree-sitter-test"
devtools::load_all (pkg_path)
#> ℹ Loading test
bodies <- test::get_captures (path)
length (bodies)
#> [1] 36
```

<sup>Created on 2024-10-02 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

The only function it's calling is this:

``` r
QUERY_FUNCTIONS <- r"(
  (binary_operator
      lhs: (identifier) @name
      operator: "<-"
      rhs: (function_definition) @fn
  )
)"
QUERY_FUNCTIONS <- treesitter::query (treesitter.r::language (), QUERY_FUNCTIONS)

#' Get treesitter captures
#'
#' @export
get_captures <- function (path) {
    path_r <- fs::path (path, "R")
    paths <- fs::dir_ls (path_r, regexp = "\\.(r|R)$")
    paths <- as.character (paths)

    parser <- treesitter::parser (treesitter.r::language ())

    lapply (paths, function (path) {
        text <- brio::read_file (path)

        tree <- treesitter::parser_parse (parser, text)
        node <- treesitter::tree_root_node (tree)

        treesitter::query_captures (QUERY_FUNCTIONS, node)
    })
}
```

I guess there's something happening here with tracking and resetting the node pointers? I'd really appreciate any insight you could give; thanks!

---

Oh, and this behaviour is only seen when the function is embedded within a package namespace, hence my construction of test repo to demonstrate. You won't see the same if you try to locally step through `r-tree-sitter` code. Everything works then too, which makes it quite tricky to debug.

title: #eq? predicate returns non-exact matches for substrings of predicate string
description:
I would not have expected `my` to match this query for definitions. It should be only `my_function` right?

``` r
  library(treesitter)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'treesitter'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     range
  library(treesitter.r)

  language <- treesitter.r::language()
  parser <- parser(language)


  tree <- parser_parse(parser,
  "
    my_function <- function(arg1, ag2) {
      arg1 + arg2
    }

    my <- function(arg1, arg2) {
      arg1 + arg2
    }

    your_function <- function(arg1, arg2) {
    arg1 + arg2
    }
  ")

def_query_source <-
  '(binary_operator
    lhs: (identifier) @lhs
    operator: ["<-" "="]
    rhs: _ @rhs
    (#eq? @lhs "my_function")
  )'

tree_query <-
  query(language, def_query_source)

tree_query_matches <-
  query_matches(tree_query, tree_root_node(tree))

length(tree_query_matches[[1]])
#> [1] 2

tree_query_matches[[1]][[1]]$node[[1]]
#> <tree_sitter_node>
#> 
#> ── Text ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> my_function
#> 
#> ── S-Expression ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> (identifier [(1, 4), (1, 15)])

tree_query_matches[[1]][[2]]$node[[1]]
#> <tree_sitter_node>
#> 
#> ── Text ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> my
#> 
#> ── S-Expression ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> (identifier [(5, 4), (5, 6)])
```

<sup>Created on 2025-04-03 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

I believe this issue is arising here:

https://github.com/DavisVaughan/r-tree-sitter/blob/4a2467ea13974a3dca0e705d9f85444e06940269/src/query-matches.c#L630-L635

Since the implementation uses `str_equal_up_to` where the size parameter to match up to comes from the length of the node text. The effect of this being that nodes that have text which is a substring of the predicate string will be matched.

title: Vignette idea - comparing finding `recipe()` calls with walk approach vs query approach
Include other languages?
description:
Hi @DavisVaughan, thanks so much for your great tree-sitter work. For an upcoming project at rOpenSci, we aim to use tree-sitter s-expression output to quantify aspects of tree edit distances between codebases, for which this package already has [all the code we need](https://github.com/DavisVaughan/r-tree-sitter/blob/d655234399c9dbf489a57e0416e251ae8b8d99df/src/node.c#L6-L17), but for R only. For our work, we need to  to overcome this limitation:
https://github.com/DavisVaughan/r-tree-sitter/blob/d655234399c9dbf489a57e0416e251ae8b8d99df/README.md?plain=1#L29-L31
and expand the functionality of this package  to the other tree-sitter languages.

Obviously you're thinking about this issue, and working on https://github.com/DavisVaughan/r-tree-sitter/blob/main/R/standalone-language.R. That suggests that there are plans to  expand R bindings to https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-c, https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-typescript, https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-julia, and/or https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-python, plus rust via the main repo. Any info on current status and vision would be very much appreciated. Thanks for this extremely useful package, which is already the best-documented and most functionally developed extension outside `api.c`!!

title: Some performance improvement opportunities
description:
- Consider `class = FALSE` (optionally?) for `TreeCursor`. This would actually make quite a big difference, as avoiding the S3 method overhead does seem to help a lot (see #21). Maybe we could expose both `TreeCursor` and `TreeCursorBare` or something for the performance cases. The idea is that in a `TreeCursor` you are often iterating over an entire tree, which has many `TreeCursor$` calls.
- Optimize `new_node()` slightly since it is called by `TreeCursor$node()`
- Optimize `check_node()` as much as we can since its called so often
- Optimizing `parser_reparse()` internals, since it can be called a lot. Can we get out of the way with our error checking? Or move it to C?

title: Deal with rlang lib API restrictions
Set `text` in a tree to `NULL` after a `tree_edit()`
description:
Editing the tree bounds results in altered start/stop bounds that no longer match the text, so we should unset the text field and have special support in the print method for this case.

We should also add checks in some of the `tree_` functions to check if we have valid text or not before proceeding.

This should be easier now because trees are immutable, so we don't need to worry about modifying a tree that has state that is also captured inside of an existing node

Run this and try and print out `tree`, it will error right now

```r
#' language <- treesitter.r::language()
#' parser <- parser(language)
#'
#' text <- "1 + foo"
#' tree <- parser_parse(parser, text)
#' tree
#'
#' text <- "1 + bar(foo)"
#' tree <- tree_edit(
#'   tree,
#'   start_byte = 4,
#'   start_point = point(0, 4),
#'   old_end_byte = 7,
#'   old_end_point = point(0, 7),
#'   new_end_byte = 12,
#'   new_end_point = point(0, 12)
#' )
```
